from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Bernoulli Trial", [
            "A Bernoulli trial has two outcomes.",
            "Success and failure are defined.",
            "Probability p is always constant."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        trial_node = Dot(color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(trial_node, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(trial_node))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Success path
        success_path = Line(self.grid['C2'], self.grid['B4'], color=GREEN)
        success_label = Text("Success", color=GREEN, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(success_label, 'B5')
        
        # Failure path
        failure_path = Line(self.grid['C2'], self.grid['D4'], color=RED)
        failure_label = Text("Failure", color=RED, font_size=20)
        self.place_at_grid(failure_label, 'D5')
        
        self.play(Create(success_path), Create(failure_path), Write(success_label), Write(failure_label))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        p_label = MathTex("p", color=GREEN, font_size=24)
        q_label = MathTex("q", color=RED, font_size=24)
        
        p_label.next_to(success_path.get_midpoint(), UP, buff=0.1)
        q_label.next_to(failure_path.get_midpoint(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(Write(p_label), Write(q_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Defining the Binomial Distribution", [
            "Use B(n, p) notation.", 
            "Trials must be independent events.", 
            "Number of trials is fixed."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        formula = MathTex(r"X \sim B(n, p)").set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B3', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)
        
        trials = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=WHITE) for _ in range(5)])
        trials.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        self.place_in_area(trials, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.add(trials)
        
        for trial in trials:
            self.play(Indicate(trial, color=GREEN), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        count_text = Text("Successes: X = 0", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(count_text, 'E3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(count_text))
        
        # Simulate counting successes
        for i in range(1, 4):
            new_text = Text(f"Successes: X = {i}", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
            new_text.move_to(count_text.get_center())
            self.play(Transform(count_text, new_text), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Formula calculates exact success probability.",
            "C(n,k) counts total success arrangements.",
            "p^k defines success probability.",
            "(1-p)^(n-k) defines failure.",
            "Graph shows success likelihood distribution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Binomial Formula: The Logic of Combinations", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        formula = MathTex(r"P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        comb = MathTex(r"\binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}")
        self.place_at_grid(comb, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(formula.copy(), comb))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        pk = MathTex(r"p^k")
        pk.set_color(BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(pk, "E2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(pk))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        qnk = MathTex(r"(1-p)^{n-k}")
        qnk.set_color(RED)
        self.place_at_grid(qnk, "E5", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(FadeIn(qnk))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[0, 0.4, 0.1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        bar_chart = BarChart(values=[0.01, 0.05, 0.12, 0.2, 0.25, 0.2, 0.12, 0.05, 0.01], bar_names=[str(i) for i in range(9)])
        graph = VGroup(axes, bar_chart).scale(0.3)
        self.place_in_area(graph, "C1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(formula), FadeOut(comb), FadeOut(pk), FadeOut(qnk))
        self.play(Create(graph))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculate 3 successes in 5 trials.",
            "Changing p shifts graph center.",
            "Robot inspects microchips for defects.",
            "Probability changes with p value.",
            "Distribution reveals defect likelihood."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Robot Quality Control", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show 10 robots, coloring defective ones red (#FF0000)
        # Create 10 robots (circles)
        robots = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, fill_opacity=1, fill_color=BLUE) for _ in range(10)])

        self.play(FadeIn(robots))

        # Defective one

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        # Placeholder for calculation visualization
        formula = MathTex(r"P(X=k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}", font_size=32)

outline.topic: Mastering Binomial Distributions: From Coin Flips to Success

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Bernoulli Trial
sections.content: Define a Bernoulli trial as an experiment with exactly two outcomes (Success/Failure) and a constant probability 'p'. Visualize this as a single path split in a decision tree.
sections.example: A smart-home sensor checking if a door is 'Locked' (p=0.8) or 'Unlocked' (q=0.2).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Distribution
sections.content: Introduce the B(n, p) notation. Explain the four requirements (BINS): Binary outcomes, Independent trials, Number of trials is fixed, and Success probability is constant.
sections.example: A squirrel gathering 10 nuts; each nut has a 50% chance of being an acorn. n=10, p=0.5.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula: The Logic of Combinations
sections.content: Break down the formula P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Explain that C(n,k) counts the ways to arrange 'k' successes, and p^k(1-p)^(n-k) defines the probability of one specific sequence.
sections.example: Visualizing a probability histogram where the bars show the likelihood of getting exactly 0 to 10 successes, forming the characteristic 'bell-like' shape.

sections.title: Application: The Robot Quality Control
sections.content: Calculate the probability of exactly 3 successes in 5 trials using the formula. Demonstrate how changing 'p' shifts the center of gravity of the distribution graph.
sections.example: A factory robot inspects 5 microchips. If each chip has a 10% defect rate (failure), what is the probability of finding exactly 1 defective chip?

sections.title: Summary & Real-World Utility
sections.content: Recap the mean (np) and variance (npq). Briefly mention how this distribution acts as a foundation for hypothesis testing and predicting rare events.
sections.example: Predicting the number of successful deliveries a drone makes in a fleet of 50, given a known success rate per flight.
